claims.claim: Clement of Alexandria (Titus Flavius Clemens) was a Greek Christian theologian who served as presbyter and head of the Catechetical School of Alexandria in the late second and early third centuries (c. 147‑215 AD).
He was born either in Alexandria or Athens and died around 215 AD in Jerusalem, Syria Palaestina.
The homily was addressed to Christian brethren, urging them not to flatter the rich and to seek salvation through proper conduct.
It was written to counter a contemporary tendency among some Christians to praise wealthy individuals and to clarify the Gospel teaching that wealth can hinder salvation.
The controversy it tackles concerns the moral danger of wealth and the question "Who can be saved?" raised by Jesus' sayings about rich people.
A 1901 printed edition of the homily was produced by the Society for Promoting Christian Knowledge, showing its transmission in modern scholarship.
